findings.problem: At 1280 and 1440 the reversibility bar renders on top of the 79. b.css:636 takes the bar out of flow with position:absolute; top:16px, and the comment above it explains that .b-edit is deliberately left unpositioned because the base rule is position:fixed. But inside the rail b.css:949 resets .b-edit to position:static, so at exactly the two widths where the editor is the rail there is no positioned ancestor and the bar escapes to .b-stick, which is sticky and therefore the containing block. Driving owner-flight at 1440, scrolled 600, open a moment and press +7: .b-undo paints at viewport (202,40) 328x62 with an opaque rgb(17,17,17) fill, while .b-num sits at (186,63) 164x127. elementFromPoint(300,100) returns .b-undo, elementFromPoint(300,120) returns .b-num: the bar covers the top 39px of the numeral and slices the caps off both digits. Meanwhile .b-edit still carries padding-top:78px reserving a band the bar never enters, which is the unexplained void at the top of the editor card in the owner-editing frame. So the one designed moment in the product mutilates the one object the whole page is built around, and pays 78px of empty card for the privilege. The behaviour gate cannot see it: the plate exists, is live and names its key, all still true. Below 1280 .b-edit is fixed and the bar is correct, which is why the phone frames look right.
findings.fix: In b.css:949 change .b-editHost .b-edit { position: static } to position: relative. Relative keeps the panel in flow in the rail exactly as static did and restores the containing block, so the bar lands in its own reserved band; the phone and tablet sheet keep the base position:fixed and are untouched. Then raise .b-edit { padding-top: 78px } (b.css:635) to 94px, because .b-undo is 70px tall at two lines (top:16 plus 70 plus its 10px rule gap) and 78 leaves the second line sitting on WHAT IT IS. Verified: with position:relative the measured overlap between .b-undo and .b-num is 0 at 1440, 1280, 768 and 390, the bar renders 17px inside the editor card, and no row in the measure moves.

findings.problem: The guest desk surface is composed for an editor it will never host. At 1440 .b-two is 360px 642px, .b-stick is 360x328 and the row it sits in is 1399 tall, so 360x1071 is empty: 34% of the 1066px composition, for 77% of its height, permanently, because .b-stick is sticky and nothing on this surface can ever fill it. On the owner surface that column earns itself the moment a moment is opened; on desk and print there is no editor, no undo and, by the lock, nothing else that belongs there. The evidence is the 1279 render: one pixel narrower the same state is a single column, the horizon and the measure share one left edge, the 79 reads against the full width of the sheet and the plan reads as one continuous instrument. The guest artifact gets worse as the window gets bigger, and it gets worse at exactly the width where the OWNER needs a rail. Round 2's refuter closed the finding that proposed filling this column and named the remedy itself: size the guest track to its placard. Narrowing alone does not pay - I swept 360 down to 300 and the void barely moves while Saturday 3 October 2026 breaks to two lines below 336px.
findings.fix: Give the audience artifact its own hook and drop the second track on it. In render-b.js states.desk (line 848) change the field call to field([...], ".b-audience"); field() already takes an extra class (render-b.js 282). Then in b.css, inside the @media (min-width: 1280px) block, add: [data-medium="full"] .b-audience .b-two { grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr); gap: 0 } and [data-medium="full"] .b-audience .b-stick { position: static }. Owner-flight, owner-editing and publish keep the rail untouched because they do not carry .b-audience. Verified at 1440: .b-two becomes one 1066px track, the row copy goes from 518 to 942, the horizon and the measure share the x187 edge, and the document grows 1680 to 2009 - the guest scrolls one more screen and gets the 1279 composition at every width above it.

findings.problem: The A4 keepsake is a fixed physical artifact whose column count is decided by the browser window it happened to be previewed in. The only rule that gives .b-print two columns sits inside @media (min-width: 1280px), so the same sheet is two different documents: at 1279 and below it is one column, no title wraps, and .b-field is 1634px tall against an A4 field of 1273 - it no longer fits the page; at 1280 and above it is 300px 316px, fits one page, and starves the measure. In the two-column form .b-copy is 192px wide and two of the seven titles break to two lines on the printed sheet (Menu tasting at / The Orchard, Choose the / evening music) while a 300x716 block of the same sheet - 30% of the live area - is blank. The most permanent thing this product makes is the one whose proportions were never decided.
findings.fix: Move the sheet's grid off the viewport and onto the sheet, and rebalance it. Delete [data-medium="sheet"] .b-two from the @media (min-width: 1280px) block in b.css and add, unconditionally: .b-print { container-type: inline-size } and @container (min-width: 640px) { .b-print .b-two { grid-template-columns: 220px minmax(0, 1fr); gap: 48px; align-items: start } }. Verified across 390, 768, 1024, 1279, 1440 and 1920: from 1024 up, wherever the stage reaches the true 794px A4 width, the sheet is identical at every viewport - tracks 220px 396px, .b-copy 272px, all seven titles on one line, .b-field 1273px so it still fits one page; below that the stage is narrower than A4 and the single column is a preview rather than the artifact.

findings.problem: The loading frame is 388x329 and what arrives is 388x1658. The skeleton reserves the horizon and stops: no DAYS AWAY head, no origin rule, no rail, not one row, so five sixths of the surface's real geometry is unreserved and the frame quintuples on resolve. The comment at 1050 argues the measure is not drawn because tick positions come from the dates, and that half is right - inventing tick positions would be a picture of a plan nobody has. But the parts that are known before the data lands are the column head, the origin rule, the rail's left offset and the height of one row, and none of them are reserved either. The four bars that are drawn are not the real geometry: 120x11 stands in for a 346x17 line, 180x82 for a 107x83 numeral, 64% x 20 for a 346x26 line. A guest opening the link on a phone sees a small card and then the page jumps to five times its height.
findings.fix: In states.loading, size the four skeleton bars to the real objects they stand for (346x17, 107x83, 346x26, 346x23, taken from the same horizon() call the real state uses), and after the Bringing in what is ahead. line append the measure's known frame: the DAYS AWAY head at its real 84px gutter width, the 1px origin rule at the same x as .b-origin, a 1px var(--fore-16) rail at left:100px running 320px down, and exactly one 74px row band - the reserve floor, one row and never two. Invent no tick and no count. That reserves roughly 500px of the arriving 1040px measure without asserting a single date.

findings.problem: The wedding-morning screen runs two alignment systems and two left edges inside 344px. .b-dayWrap is padding: 56px 22px 40px with text-align: center, so MARA & FINN, Today, the date and the sentence all sit on x570 and are centred; .b-dayNow, .b-behind and .b-foot sit on x548 and are left-aligned. The two rules on the screen disagree about where its edges are: .b-dayRule is max-width 200px, centred, indigo; the section rules under it are 344px full-bleed hairlines. Twenty-two pixels and a change of axis, four times, on the one screen in the product that is pure feeling and has nothing else in it to look at. The eye lands on Today correctly and then the composition tells it the page has moved.
findings.fix: Keep the centred masthead - it is right for that screen - and make everything on it obey one edge. Set .b-dayWrap padding to 56px 0 40px so its content shares the x548 field edge with every section below it, and change .b-dayRule to width: 200px; margin: 0 auto 24px so the rule stays 200px and centred within that full-width block. Then centre the rest of the screen with it: add text-align: center to .b-dayNow and to .b-behind's summary row for state=day only, and set the day screen's .b-foot to the same centred axis, so the morning screen is one centred column top to bottom instead of a centred head on a left-aligned ledger.

biggestWin: The measure is award-winning and should be treated as settled. One scale per medium, a marked origin, tabular counts in their own 84px gutter, a hairline that is a real axis, and position that genuinely is the quantity - I checked it at every size and the proportion between one gap and the next is identical at 10, 12, 14 and 18 pixels a day. The single-column form of the whole page, which is what runs at 1279 and below, is the best composition in the artifact: the horizon and the measure share one edge and the plan reads as one instrument. Nothing above asks to change any of that. What stands between this and 9.5 is that the surfaces around the instrument have not caught up with it. Three of the five defects are one CSS declaration each and are already verified in the browser: the reversibility bar needs position: relative instead of static so it stops printing over the 79; the guest desk needs the owner's rail taken off it, because the guest artifact is currently worse at 1440 than at 1279; the A4 keepsake needs its grid driven by the sheet rather than by the window, because today it is a different document depending on the screen it was previewed on, and in its two-column form it wraps titles on the printed page while 30% of the sheet is blank. Only the loading skeleton and the morning screen are real work, and both are small. This is polish plus two half-day builds in files that already exist - call it a day and a half total, no architectural move, no new decision. The score is below round 2's because the remediation that put the reversibility bar in the right place in the markup put it in the wrong place on the screen at the owner's own two widths, and because the guest composition the round-2 refuter itself flagged went untouched. The instrument is a 9; the pages it is set in are a 7.
